22:#include "torture.h"
23:#include "libopensc/log.c"
24:#include "libopensc/asn1.c"
25:
26:/* The last argument is an OID value */
27:#define TORTURE_OID(name, asn1_data, ...) \
28:     static void torture_asn1_oid_## name (void **state) \
29:     { \
30:             u8 data[] = asn1_data; \
31:             size_t datalen = sizeof(data) - 1; \
32:             struct sc_object_id ref_oid = {{__VA_ARGS__}}; \
33:             struct sc_object_id oid; \
34:             int rv; \
35:             u8 *buf = NULL; \
36:             size_t buflen = 0; \
37:     \
38:             rv = sc_asn1_decode_object_id(data, datalen, &oid); \
39:             assert_int_equal(rv, SC_SUCCESS); \
40:             assert_int_equal(sc_compare_oid(&ref_oid, &oid), 1); /* XXX */ \
41:             rv = sc_asn1_encode_object_id(&buf, &buflen, &oid); \
42:             assert_int_equal(rv, SC_SUCCESS); \
43:             assert_int_equal(buflen, datalen); \
44:             assert_memory_equal(buf, data, buflen); \
45:             free(buf); \
46:     }
47:#define TORTURE_OID_ERROR(name, asn1_data, error) \
48:     static void torture_asn1_oid_## name (void **state) \
49:     { \
50:             u8 data[] = asn1_data; \
51:             size_t datalen = sizeof(data) - 1; \
52:             struct sc_object_id oid; \
53:             int rv; \
54:     \
55:             rv = sc_asn1_decode_object_id(data, datalen, &oid); \
56:             assert_int_equal(rv, error); \
57:     }
58:
59:/* Without the tag (0x06) and length */
60:/* Small OID values */
61:TORTURE_OID(small, "\x01\x02\x03\x04\x05\x06", 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, -1)
62:/* Limit what we can fit into the first byte */
63:TORTURE_OID(limit, "\x7F", 2, 47, -1)
64:/* The second octet already overflows to the second byte */
65:TORTURE_OID(two_byte, "\x81\x00", 2, 48, -1)
66:/* Existing OID ec publickey */
67:TORTURE_OID(ecpubkey, "\x2A\x86\x48\xCE\x3D\x02\x01", 1, 2, 840, 10045, 2, 1, -1)
68:
69:/* Negative tests */
70:/* Missing second byte, even though indicated with the first bit */
71:TORTURE_OID_ERROR(missing, "\x81", SC_ERROR_INVALID_ASN1_OBJECT)
72:/* Missing second byte in later identifiers */
73:TORTURE_OID_ERROR(missing_second, "\x2A\x48\x81", SC_ERROR_INVALID_ASN1_OBJECT)
74:/* Non-minimal encoding of first part */
75:TORTURE_OID_ERROR(non_minimal_second, "\x2A\x80\x01", SC_ERROR_INVALID_ASN1_OBJECT)
76:/* Non-minimal encoding of first part */
77:TORTURE_OID_ERROR(non_minimal, "\x80\x01", SC_ERROR_INVALID_ASN1_OBJECT)
78:
79:/*
80: * Test undefined behavior of too large parts of OID encoding
81: *
82: * The specification does not place any limits to these values, but they
83: * are internally in opensc stored as ints so it makes sense to reject
84: * the too-large onese for now, rather than causing undefined overflow.
85: *
86: * https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase-detail/5673497895895040
87: */
88:#if INT_MAX == 2147483647
89:/* 2.5.4.2147483647 (The last part is largest 32 bit integer) */
90:TORTURE_OID(last_int_max, "\x55\x04\x87\xFF\xFF\xFF\x7F", 2, 5, 4, 2147483647, -1)
91:/* 2.2147483647.4.3 (The second part is largest 32 bit integer) */
92:TORTURE_OID(first_int_max, "\x88\x80\x80\x80\x4F\x04\x03", 2, 2147483647, 4, 3, -1)
93:#else
94:/* 2.5.4.2147483647 (The last part is largest 32 bit integer) */
95:TORTURE_OID_ERROR(last_int_max, "\x55\x04\x87\xFF\xFF\xFF\x7F", SC_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED)
96:/* 2.2147483647.4.3 (The second part is largest 32 bit integer) */
97:TORTURE_OID_ERROR(first_int_max, "\x88\x80\x80\x80\x4F\x04\x03", SC_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED)
98:#endif
99:
100:/* 2.5.4.2147483648 (The last part is 32 bit integer overflow) */
101:TORTURE_OID_ERROR(last_32b_overflow, "\x55\x04\x88\x80\x80\x80\x00", SC_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED)
102:/* 2.2147483648.4.3 (The second part is 32 bit integer overflow) */
103:TORTURE_OID_ERROR(first_32b_overflow, "\x88\x80\x80\x80\x50\x04\x03", SC_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED)
104:/* TODO SC_MAX_OBJECT_ID_OCTETS */
105:
106:#define TORTURE_INTEGER(name, asn1_data, int_value) \
107:    static void torture_asn1_integer_## name (void **state) \
108:    { \
109:            u8 data[] = asn1_data; \
110:            size_t datalen = sizeof(data) - 1; \
111:            int value = 0; \
112:            int rv; \
113:            u8 *buf = NULL; \
114:            size_t buflen = 0; \
115:    \
116:            rv = sc_asn1_decode_integer(data, datalen, &value, 1); \
117:            assert_int_equal(rv, SC_SUCCESS); \
118:            assert_int_equal(value, int_value); \
119:            rv = asn1_encode_integer(value, &buf, &buflen); \
120:            assert_int_equal(rv, SC_SUCCESS); \
